chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wasshash, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not proper for a man to give butter as a loan in exchange for oil, nor to give oil as a loan in exchange for butter.'

key_terms.إِسْلاَفُ: Giving a loan of a commodity to be repaid with another commodity
key_terms.بِالزَّيْتِ: With oil (specifically olive oil or similar)
key_terms.لاَ يَنْبَغِي: It is not proper / not permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging butter for oil in a loan transaction in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the specific prohibition of *islaf* (loan for loan) between butter and oil, reflecting the Shia juristic concern for preventing hidden usury (*riba*) through subtle discrepancies in quality or measurement. It underscores the principle of fairness in commodity exchanges, ensuring that equivalent value is maintained to avoid disputes in commercial transactions.
